claims: Active auroral conditions (Kp 4) are forecasted for mid-March 2026.
Potential visibility of aurora in northern U.S. states and high-latitude regions is forecasted for mid-March 2026.
A G1 (Minor) storm is possible due to solar winds.
A G1 (Minor) storm would make the northern lights visible low on the horizon as far south as parts of the US northern tier.
Forecasted aurora visibility area for March 15-16, 2026 includes Northern US (WA, MT, ND, MN, WI, MI, ME), Alaska, Canada, and Northern Europe.
Forecasted aurora intensity for March 15-16, 2026 is Active (Kp 4).
Highest auroral activity is typically in late evening (10 PM to 2 AM local time).
NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center offers a 30-minute forecast to see the currently forecasted auroral oval.
Geophysical Institute at UAF offers localized forecasts, particularly for Alaska.
"My Aurora Forecast & Alerts" provides real-time alerts.
